_comment: MCP servers Alil can reach via the on-demand mcp.* meta-tools. Tools are NEVER injected into context; the model discovers them with mcp.search → mcp.inspect → mcp.call. Empty `servers` (the default) means MCP is off. Each entry: { name, transport: 'stdio'|'http'|'sse', command, args?, env?, url?, headers?, guardUrls?, timeoutMs?, minEffect?, enabled?, tools? }. Streamable-HTTP servers use transport:'http' + url; legacy HTTP+SSE servers use transport:'sse'. `headers` values may reference ${ENV_VAR} (resolved from .env at connect time, so secrets never live here). `guardUrls: true` is for servers that fetch URLs for Alil (crawlers): every URL argument must be http(s) and resolve to a public address before the call, the same SSRF check web.fetch makes. `enabled` defaults true; set it false (or toggle it in the MCP UI tab) to make a server fully invisible to the model — dropped from search, refused by inspect/call. `tools` pins a classification per tool name, e.g. { "get_quote": { "effect": "read", "risk": "low" } } lets that tool run without approval, { "place_order": { "effect": "spend", "risk": "critical" } } makes it always ask fresh. Unpinned tools stay execute/high; a server's own readOnlyHint never lowers that.
